newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Eurodollars wary ahead U.S. jobs data.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Eurodollars wary ahead U.S. jobs data.

text.p: SIMEX Eurodollar futures ended firmer on Thursday as players adjusted their positions ahead of the release of the U.S. August employment report due on Friday.
While the market consensus calls for an increase of 250,000 non-farm jobs in August, dealers were divided on the report's possible impact on U.S. treasuries.
"The number of new jobs created is pretty high already so even if (Friday's) number is less than expected, the market could still come off," said a trader with a U.S. futures house.

But a trader with a European institution said the recent spate of positive U.S. economic indicators, including durable goods, consumer confidence and the Chicago Purchasing Management Index, only represented "pockets of strength".
"If payrolls comes out at 150,000, the market will have to reprice," he said, adding that the market had overstretched itself by discounting a 50 basis point interest rate hike.
"The Federal Reserve has tolerated a figure of over 200,000 for the past few months, why should they suddenly hike by 50 basis points?"
After trading in a four-point band, December Eurodollars ended at 93.88 against their IMM close at 93.87 on moderate volume of 13,810 lots.
Euroyen futures finished slightly weaker on the back of a rise in Nikkei futures and softer Japanese government bond (JGB) futures.
The September Nikkei contract bounced back from its recent lows -- inspired by the tension between the United States and Iraq -- to touch a high of 21,500.
"I don't see Euroyen futures breaking out of their ranges unless there are developments on monetary policy in the U.S. and Japan," said a trader with an Asian house.
December Euroyen finished at unchanged against its CME close at 99.26. March was at 99.06 against 99.08.
